task.description: Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's output for REQ-036. Read lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary). Read REQ-036's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml first. Pay particular attention to Section 9 (Open questions) -- CODE-DESIGNER flagged 4 real data-model gaps: no permission-string concept in REQ-020's model (9.1, no built-in default for opts[:permission_checker]), no tenant production/test classification column (9.2, flagged default: classify-all-as-:test via opts[:tenant_classifier]), variable_schemas never ported (9.3, safe always-nil default), process_definitions.version free-form text with unconfirmed > semantics (9.4, flagged numeric-else-lexicographic fallback). Independently judge whether each of these is a legitimate flagged default (stated, reasoned, not scope creep) versus a silent guess or an unacceptable resolution -- do not just accept CODE-DESIGNER's own framing without checking the actual source files it cites (lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex, tenant_role.ex, group.ex, tenant.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex).
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-036's 6 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete design element with no TBD/deferral
All 3 modules' function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases)
Error handling shape stated explicitly ({:ok,_}|{:error,_} tags, not left implicit)
No implementation code present (no .ex code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only)
Independently verify the 4 open-question defaults in Section 9 against the actual source files cited, not just CODE-DESIGNER's summary of them
Independently verify the permission_checker default (9.1) is genuinely NOT a silently-invented enforcement mechanism -- it must have no built-in default per the design
